sections.h2: Where is Salem, Massachusetts, and how is it arranged?
sections.html:
Salem is a historic harbor city in Essex County on the North Shore, about 15 miles northeast of downtown Boston. Wikipedia gives its 2020 population as 44,480 and its total area as 18.3 square miles, of which more than half is water.

Water cuts the city into small pieces. Salem Harbor separates it from Marblehead, Beverly Harbor and the Danvers River separate it from Beverly, and the North and South rivers divide the neighborhoods. Beverly, Danvers, Peabody, Lynn, Swampscott and Marblehead all touch its borders.

Salem was one of the two county seats of Essex County until county government was dissolved in 1999.

sections.h2: How does Salem's history affect houses and sales?
sections.html:
Few Massachusetts cities carry as much preservation weight. Salem was a leading seaport in early American trade, and the 1692 witch trials still define its public image. Two of its historic residential areas, the Federal Street District and the Charter Street Historic District, are named on Wikipedia, and Chestnut Street is known for its Federal architecture.

The Great Salem Fire of 1914 destroyed more than 400 homes and left 3,500 families homeless, yet it spared the Chestnut Street block of Federal houses. That is part of why Salem has older neighborhoods beside areas rebuilt in the early 1900s.

If your house is in an historic district, ask the city's planning office before you plan exterior changes or a teardown. We did not open a Salem page on historic district rules, so this page does not describe them.

sections.h2: Which Salem neighborhoods should sellers know?
sections.html:
Wikipedia describes Salem as divided by its natural features into small neighborhoods:

  • Downtown: the historic core of the city, 15 miles northeast of Boston.
  • Salem Neck and Winter Island: a peninsula northeast of downtown, with a 30-acre Winter Island Park.
  • North Salem: west of the Neck, across the North River.
  • South Salem: south of the South River and mostly along the banks of Salem Harbor.

Water separates these areas, so a house a few blocks away across a river can feel like a different neighborhood to buyers.

sections.h2: What do Salem's economy, university and schools look like?
sections.html:
Wikipedia calls Salem today a residential and tourist area. Salem State University, the largest of the nine campuses in the state university system, enrolls more than 10,000 undergraduate and graduate students and houses about 2,000 of them in campus residence halls.

Tourism around the witch trials is large, though Wikipedia notes residents have debated how much the city should rely on it. For a house owner, the tourism question is also a rules question, covered in the next section.

Public elementary schools include Bates, Carlton, Horace Mann, Saltonstall and Witchcraft Heights, with Collins Middle School and Salem High School. Two charter schools, Salem Academy and Bentley Academy, are also public.

sections.h2: What else shapes Salem's identity and its land?
sections.html:
Salem's story is bigger than 1692. Wikipedia notes that the National Guard first mustered on Salem Common in 1636, and during the Revolutionary War the port became a center of privateering, with about 1,700 Letters of Marque granted. Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote about the area in the 19th century.

Winter Island, on Salem Neck, once held a Coast Guard air station that moved to Cape Cod in 1970. The island is now a 30-acre city park. Gallows Hill is a city park too, and Proctor's Ledge, identified in 2016 as the site of the executions, is a memorial.

These public lands, plus the harbor frontage, limit how much of the city can ever be built on. A smaller land base is part of what you are selling into.

sections.h2: How do you get in and out of Salem?
sections.html:
Salem has its own station on the MBTA Commuter Rail's Newburyport/Rockport Line. Routes 1A, 114 and 107 pass through the city, and Route 1A uses the Veterans Memorial Bridge to Beverly.

There is no highway inside the city. The closest access to Route 128 is along Route 114 in Peabody, which is worth stating up front in a listing, since some buyers assume a highway exit is close.

A former rail line toward Marblehead has been turned into a bike path, and the city has discussed a possible South Salem rail station on Ocean Avenue West.

sections.h2: What are Salem's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Salem regulates short-term rentals more tightly than most Massachusetts cities, and that matters if you own a house that has been listed on Airbnb or a similar site. According to the City of Salem short-term rental page, the City Council adopted ordinances in 2018 that require:

  • Annual registration of the rental with the city.
  • A Certificate of Fitness.
  • For a property that is not the owner's primary residence, a special permit from the Zoning Board of Appeals and registration for the non-owner-occupied trash fee.
  • Collection of the state and local room occupancy excise tax.

The page states that new non-owner-occupied short-term rentals are not permitted, and that the special permit path applies only to properties that were operating as short-term rentals before July 16, 2018. Zoning also limits the use to certain neighborhoods.

For a seller, that rule can decide what a buyer may do with the house. If you bought a house as a short-term rental, confirm its registration and permit status with the city before you list it.

sections.h2: What does a Salem seller have to do before closing?
sections.html:
Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department, showing smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the rules for a sale or transfer. The state says to call the fire department as soon as you have a closing date, that alarms with no date stamp count as expired, and that a fee applies. Details are on the Mass.gov alarm page.

The deed excise tax is set by G.L. c. 64D, section 1, which names a base rate of $2 for each $500 of consideration. We did not open the registry that records Salem deeds, so ask your attorney for the current rate and the recording fee.

We also could not open a Salem page on tax due dates, so check the dates printed on your bill or call the assessor's office.

sections.h2: How can you contest a Salem assessment?
sections.html:
A tax abatement is a reduction granted when your house's fair cash value is lower than its assessed value. State law sets a short path:

  1. Pay your tax installments on time.
  2. File the approved abatement application with the assessors by the first installment due date on your bill.
  3. Assessors have three months to act, and silence counts as a denial.
  4. Appeal to the Appellate Tax Board within three months of the decision.

Valuation is as of January 1 before the fiscal year. The Appellate Tax Board's guide describes each step.

sections.h2: What are your choices if you want to sell a Salem house quickly?
sections.html:
The three routes are listing, selling on your own, or accepting a cash offer. A listing suits a house in good shape in a sought-after area. A cash sale suits a house that needs repairs, an inherited property or a landlord who wants out.

In Salem, extra items can add time: a historic district review for exterior work, a short-term rental permit transfer question, or a certificate delay at the fire department. Spotting them early lets you pick the route that avoids the slowest steps.

faqs.q: What county is Salem, MA in?
faqs.a: Salem is in Essex County, on the North Shore of Greater Boston.

faqs.q: Why is Salem called the Witch City?
faqs.a: The nickname comes from the 1692 Salem witch trials, which still shape the city's identity, tourism and even its school team names.

faqs.q: Is there a highway in Salem?
faqs.a: No. The nearest Route 128 access is along Route 114 in neighboring Peabody.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Salem?
faqs.a: Only with city registration, a Certificate of Fitness and, for a non-owner-occupied unit, a special permit. The city says new non-owner-occupied short-term rentals are not permitted.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Salem?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a local fire department certificate of compliance for the sale or transfer of a home.
